hpi_details: 63F presents with 3-month history of excruciating, lightning-fast electric shock-like stabs of pain affecting the right cheek, upper lip, and jaw. clinical_knowledge.topic: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Classic Tic Douloureux) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Trigeminal Neuralgia (Classic Tic Douloureux) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Initiate Carbamazepine 100 mg BID, titrating gradually up to 400-600 mg BID as tolerated (monitor CBC and LFTs; check HLA-B*1502 in Asian ancestry), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sharp, electric shock-like facial pain triggered by chewing, brushing teeth, and cold breeze

Key HPI features: 63F presents with 3-month history of excruciating, lightning-fast electric shock-like stabs of pain affecting the right cheek, upper lip, and jaw. Episodes last 5-15 seconds and occur dozens of times daily. Pain is reliably triggered by light touch to the face, chewing, drinking cold water, brushing teeth, or feeling a draft of wind.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 72, BP 130/80. Facial inspection normal. Neurological examination reveals intact cranial nerves without facial weakness or sustained sensory loss. Light brush of cotton swab over right nasolabial fold instantly triggers a severe 10-second grimacing spasm of right facial pain. High-resolution 3D-FIESTA brain MRI demonstrates neurovascular compression of the right trigeminal nerve root entry zone by an aberrant, tortuous loop of the superior cerebellar artery (SCA).
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Trigeminal Neuralgia (Classic Tic Douloureux).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Dental pulpitis/abscess (already excluded by extraction) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Bilateral pain or younger age of onset — should prompt MRI to exclude multiple sclerosis.
management_principles: Initiate Carbamazepine 100 mg BID, titrating gradually up to 400-600 mg BID as tolerated (monitor CBC and LFTs; check HLA-B*1502 in Asian ancestry)

If medical management fails or causes intolerable side effects, refer to neurosurgery for Microvascular Decompression (MVD - Jannetta procedure) of the right trigeminal nerve, or Gamma Knife radiosurgery
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Identify clinical criteria distinguishing Trigeminal Neuralgia from dental abscess, temporomandibular joint disorder, and cluster headache
Explain the neuroanatomical mechanism of vascular compression at the trigeminal root entry zone by the superior cerebellar artery
Select Carbamazepine as first-line pharmacotherapy and understand required lab monitoring and HLA screening guidelines
Describe surgical options including Microvascular Decompression (MVD) and ablative rhizotomy procedures

teaching.one_liner: Compression of the trigeminal nerve by a blood vessel causes brief, electric shock-like facial pain triggered by trivial touch — brushing teeth, chewing, cold air — with pain-free intervals, distinguishing it from a dental problem.
differentials: Multiple sclerosis (if bilateral or young onset)
red_flags: Bilateral pain or younger age of onset — should prompt MRI to exclude multiple sclerosis

must_ask.say: Does the pain feel like an electric shock, lasting just seconds?
Does chewing, brushing your teeth, or a cold breeze set it off?
Are you completely pain-free between attacks?
Where exactly is the pain — cheek, upper lip, jaw?
Did the tooth extractions help at all?
